_note: Manual visual assessment of 8 self-shot phone photos of real elevator panels, none from the training dataset. No ground-truth annotations exist for these, so each prediction was checked by eye against the annotated image in this directory. A reviewer can verify every count by opening the corresponding *_annotated.jpg.

per_image.note: every numbered and lettered button correct: 8,18,27 / 7,17,26 / 6,16,25 / 5,15,24 / 4,14,23 / 3,13,22 / 2,12,21 / 1,11,20 / G,10,19 / B,9. Errors confined to a wheelchair pictogram, a phone, two keyholes and a bypass switch.
1-9 and B1 all correct. Errors are door-open/close arrows, an emergency phone and two keyholes.
misreads 21->4, 14->4, 11->M, 9->2, 7->1, 1->4. Engraved metal, low contrast, strong specular glare.
3,1,2,G correct; 4 misread. The other 6 buttons are symbols (fan, light, STOP, bell, door open, door close), all given spurious digits.
3,4,2,G correct; 1 misread as 4. Keyhole correctly returned no read. The floor-indicator display was correctly NOT detected.
systematic failure. The number is engraved to the left of the button, not on it. crop_padding_ratio=-0.22 crops inward and removes the number, leaving a blank metal disc.
same panel design and same systematic failure as 14.15.57.
nothing detected. The detector was trained only on raised buttons with bezels; a flat printed surface has no edges to latch onto.

findings: Detection transfers well to real photographs. 7 of 8 panels were detected essentially completely at full phone resolution and portrait aspect, despite the model only ever seeing 640x640 squares.
Recognition is bimodal, not average. 89.0% where the label is printed on the button; 0% where it sits beside the button. The single number 49.6% describes neither regime.

Symbol buttons are always assigned a spurious text label. The classifier was trained only on OCR-scorable crops, so it has no symbol class and cannot abstain -- a fan reads as '5', STOP as 'B3'. This is a design gap, not a tuning issue.
The inward crop (-0.22) is overfitted to on-button labels. It was tuned on a dataset where every label sits on its button, and it is precisely what destroys the beside-button panels.
Flat capacitive panels are entirely out of distribution for the detector.
